evidence_packet.evidence_text: ПАВЕЛ ДЕДИЩЕВ В ЛОНДОНЕ | 30ГО СЕНТЯБРЯ | BIG BELLY COMEDY CLUB Tickets, Wednesday, September 30 • 7 PM - 9:30 PM | Eventbrite Share this event ПАВЕЛ ДЕДИЩЕВ В ЛОНДОНЕ | 30ГО СЕНТЯБРЯ | BIG BELLY COMEDY CLUB By UK STAND-UP CLUB Follow Big Belly Comedy Club Лондон, Greater London Wednesday, September 30 • 7 PM - 9:30 PM Overview Павел Дедищев выступит в Лондоне со своим стендап концертом "АМЕРИКАНЕЦ" Лондон! 30го сентября к нам приезжает Павел Дедищев со своим концертом "Американец" Резидент шоу Stand Up на ТНТ, финалист «Comedy Баттл» и «Большого шоу», участник проектов «Решалы» и «Было слово». Он стоял у истоков объединения HIT2SHIT (будущего Labelcom), стал сооснователем канала «Комьюнити» и одним из тех, кто формировал новую волну русскоязычного стендапа. Павел Дедищев - комик с ярко выраженным собственным стилем, в котором сочетаются честность, дерзость и умение подмечать детали, знакомые каждому. Его стендап строится на живых наблюдениях, бытовых историях и неожиданных поворотах, которые превращают обычные ситуации в мощные комедийные моменты. Дедищев говорит прямо, не сглаживает углы и именно этим вызывает у зрителей тот самый взрывной смех. Address: Big Belly Comedy Club, Unit 6 & 7, 30 Stamford St, London SE1 9LQ Doors: 19:00 Start: 19:45 End: 21:30 Мы работаем по принципу first come, first served, а именно, кто пришел раньше, то и занял лучшее место. 18+ P.S. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Secondary school pupils from across Greater Manchester have designed, built and competed with their own mine-detecting robots in The University of Manchester’s annual Manchester Minesweeper competition, sponsored by the Institute of Measurement Control (InstMC) Central Northwest The challenge, now in its third year, saw teams of Year 10 and 11 pupils spend four weeks developing metal-detecting robotic systems before returning to the University’s Nancy Rothwell Building for a series of live detection challenges The competition is inspired by research carried out by the University’s electromagnetic sensing team and gives young people hands-on experience of electronics engineering while highlighting the real-world challenge of detecting buried landmines and other hidden objects undergroun Teams started with an introductory workshop in June, where they received their robot kits and took part in practical engineering sessions, careers talks and got the chance to meet and ask questions to professionals from across the electrical engineering sector. They were then pai The competition culminated in a final event on 14 July, with pupils putting their creations to the test in a series of practical arena challenges designed to assess their detection and engineering skills Co-op Academy Swinton took first place overall. St Ambrose Barlow RC High School were named runners-up and Chorlton High School South received the award for ‘Best Presentation’, all receiving specially engraved trophies

evidence_packet.evidence_text: New Manchester research suggests tackling the factors behind suspensions could help prevent repeated exclusions and support vulnerable pupils School suspensions are associated with a complex combination of socioeconomic disadvantage, special educational needs, peer relationships and pupils’ experiences of school, according to new research from The University of Manchester The study analysed survey responses from more than 19,000 secondary school pupils linked to administrative records across Hampshire & Isle of Wight, to examine a wide range of factors associated with whether pupils were suspended and how often suspensions occurred Researchers found pupils receiving special educational needs (SEN) support or with an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) were more than twice as likely to be suspended than pupils without SEN, while those eligible for free school meals were also at increased risk The analysis also identified a number of factors associated with lower suspension risk, including pupils feeling that they belonged at school, being satisfied with their academic attainment, having positive relationships with school staff and having stronger emotion regulation sk By contrast, higher levels of peer pressure, experiences of bullying, and recent substance use were associated with an increased likelihood of suspension

A world first falls prevention pilot in Greater Manchester has shown that identifying older people at risk of falling and offering them early support can help improve their participation in strength and balance classes, confidence and independence.. . The eFalls pilot, launched in Wigan in February 2025, used routine NHS data to identify more than 1,100 people aged 65 and over who were at increased risk of falling in the following year.. . People identified through the pilot were contacted through their GP practice and invited for a health check, with support offered to help reduce their risk of falling.. . Almost eight in 10 people offered support chose to take part, with many going on to attend local strength and balance classes through the Falls Management Exercise (FaME) programme.. . The evaluation found that the benefits of taking part went beyond helping people improve their balance.. . Participants reported feeling stronger when getting up from a chair and walking outside, as well as having greater confidence to go out alone and less worry about falling.. . Some people also reported sleeping better, feeling brighter and enjoying being active again. The pilot also found that the way people were approached was important in encouraging them to take up the offer of support.. . evidence_packet.evidence_text: Clarice Berry died from chest injuries suffered when the gable wall of her home in in Shevington, Wigan, collapsed on to her in July 2021, trapping her beneath the rubble The 77-year-old was in the lean-to carport beneath the gable end of the property when the entirety of the gable wall and the upper part of the outer leaf of the end wall, weighing around 3,800kg, collapsed In a prevention of future deaths report published on Thursday, coroner Bronia Hartley said Berry's husband reported the bowing wall nearly eight years beforehand Hartley ruled her death could have been prevented in an inquest in July if action was taken after concerns about the wall were repeatedly raised The home was an end-of-terrace rental property owned by landlord S&G Properties (No 2) Limited and overseen by property management company KMPM From 2013 onwards, the property showed signs of cavity wall tie erosion, Hartley's report said

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A long-running legal battle over public loans worth £140m made by Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA) to a city centre developer could be heading to the Supreme Court Landowner Aubrey Weis has applied for permission to appeal against the GMCA in the ongoing dispute over loans to so-called "special purpose vehicles" - companies set up to deliver specific development projects - linked to Renaker founder Daren Whitaker The application follows attempts to overturn the earlier ruling in hearings to the Competition Appeal Tribunal and the Court of Appeal Weis's lawyers claim the loans were unfair subsidies, but the Court of Appeal ruling in June found there had been "no error of law" in the GMCA's decision to provide them Lawyers representing Weis argued earlier this year that loans made by the GMCA to Renaker were made on a "flawed and unlawful" basis and offered "unduly favourable" interest rates The funding came from the Greater Manchester Housing Investment Loans Fund (GMHILF) and supported the Trinity Islands and New Jackson developments in Manchester city centre

Captive Devices was founded in 2024 by a trio of former Epic Games engineers – including Fred Isaac (pictured) – and received support from GM Business Growth Hub’s Innovation Service in securing innovation grants . A developer of professional head-mounted camera systems and software, it enables markerless facial performance capture, used in visual effects, games and virtual production. Oxford Metrics is a smart sensing and measurement technology group serving life sciences, entertainment, engineering and manufacturing markets. The acquisition adds specialist facial capture to its platform Vicon, which has an established market leadership in body tracking. Captive Devices’ first product was CoreHMC, a head-mounted camera facial motion capture system. The technology captures real human facial expressions and translates them into digital animation data, without the cost or complexity typically associated with bespoke setups. Instead of complicated tailored camera rigs, with custom software builds, time-intensive installation and ongoing technical support, the Captive Devices concept works straight out of the box. Its founding team – who designed and built similar systems prior to founding the business – will be joining Vicon. The partnership aims to lower entry barriers for scaling businesses by providing reciprocal workspace access, market entry support, and cross-border network integration across two of Europe’s most dynamic technology hubs. Building on the 2025 Liverpool City Region and Greater Manchester Trade Mission in Dublin, the partnership aims to unlock cross-border commercial potential, strengthening the £2bn Manchester–Dublin corridor by creating clear international expansion pathways for early-stage businesses. Key features of the agreement include: Market Entry and Connections: Broadening connections to help startups access new markets, including launch events for new residents taking up permanent space and network access. Reciprocal Desk Access: Providing founders with a base to expand internationally and grow their presence in Manchester and Dublin with low to no overheads. The next phase of AI is likely to be much less about what a model can demonstrate on a screen and much more about whether businesses can deploy it securel There is also an opportunity for Manchester and the wider North that goes beyond simply increasing AI adoption. The region already has strengths across advanced materials, computing infrastructure, cyber security, health innovation and emerging technologies such as quantum. CEO Erno Hilden has said that consultations are underway regarding workforce reductions, although no figure has been decided In April 2026, AirBaltic took on a €30 million (£26 million) state loan but since then it has faced a number of financial challenges. The company said in a statement, "including increased fuel costs arising from the crisis in the Middle East."

Maureen O'Callaghan had moved to Berrycroft Manor, in Romiley , to benefit from '24-hour care' at a cost of '£1,600 a week', her family told Stockport Coron But the inquest heard how the 78-year-old, who had dementia, 'went downhill' throughout her time at the home in 2025. Maureen had previously attempted to climb out of the window and would throw items from the window on occasions Her family told coroner Jyoti Gill they had spoken to care home staff with safety concerns about the window, but nothing was done about it before her death on September 29 last year. Describing Maureen's death as a 'preventable tragedy', the family said: "She was an integral part The inquest heard how following Maureen's death, social care regulator the Care Quality Commission (CQC) has initiated criminal proceedings, but no further details were given. The court heard how Maureen had been physically fit, and enjoyed walking and swimming, but as her dement John O'Callaghan, Maureen's son, said: "From being the mum we all knew and loved, this horrible disease just got a grip of her. But the smiley little boy from Rochdale had his life cruelly cut short, aged just two, in December 2020 Prolonged exposure to mould at the social flat where his family lived led to the toddler’s death . His family had pleaded for help to fix the stubborn mould problem that refused to go away, but they did not get the support they needed Following the tragedy, the Manchester Evening News uncovered widespread issues of damp, mould and disrepair on the same estate. Comme An investigation is currently underway into why train services across the region were thrown into chaos last month . A new Bee Network report also said Avanti West Coast services were among the worst performing with cancellations doubling in July The new report, published ahead of a Bee Network committee meeting on September 24, said transport services ‘remained resilient during periods of extreme heat’. Despite the challenges , the report said it was ‘another good month’ for punctuality with both bus and Metrolink servic However rail services, which have not been taken over yet by Transport for Greater Manchester, performed worse. Problems faced included trespassing being ‘a major cause of disruption’ while crew availability continuing to be a problem All operators between June 28 to July 25 saw performance decline. Long distance operators saw the worst performance with only 42.7% of Avanti and 47% of CrossCountry trains running on time The report said Avanti was particularly hit with cancellations which more than doubled from 5.8 per cent to 12.1 pc. Jason was diagnosed with stage three multiple myeloma, a type of blood cancer, which was terminal He went on to spend five years in remission but last November several lumps were found, with tests confirming he had relapsed. Portuguese nationals Diogo Cabral, 21, and Emanuel Feliciano Simoes, 36, organised the attack on Snapchat, car "Let's do this mission today," one message discovered by detectives read. Manchester Crown Court heard they were seen pulling up in a car outside Shzsr Enterprises Ltd, on Broughton Street, Cheetham Hill at around midnight on March 1, 2023 They prised open the shutters with crowbars before two of them ran back to the car and grabbing bottles of accelerant. One of the three remained inside the building after a door was smashed and a fire started There was a 'spontaneous explosion of light and flames', prosecutor Henry Blackshaw said. The third man, who was behind the shutters, was seen on CCTV fleeing like a 'scalded cat', appearing to be on fire After the flames died down, he joined the other two in the car before it sped off. Firefigthers raced to the scene and the blaze was extinguished. Around £300,000 of damage was caused at the bedding supply business

A few years ago, Elliott Street looked like many other struggling high streets: boarded-up shopfronts, empty windows, a town that felt left behind None of this change happened by accident. It happened because a local group, 'For Tyldesley CIC', took charge of a High Street Heritage Action Zone and brought empty buildings back into use – above the shops as well as within them That's the bit we overlook. When we talk about high street decline, we talk about what's at street level – the shops coming and going. We talk far less about what sits above them: floor after floor of empty space, in some cases unused for years. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Lillia Lloyd Watson 13 from Bolton, missing girl police appeal LIVE Updated 9 mins ago Missing Lillia search LIVE as mum issues plea to Bolton girl, 13, one week after she vanished - updates An urgent appeal has again been issued for 13-year-ol The 13-year-old was last seen boarding the 247 bus at the Trafford Centre at 1.50pm on Saturday (September 12). She had been reported missing a day earlier, having been seen at Piccadilly Gardens bus station just before 11pm that night Earlier this week, her mother issued a heartfelt plea for Lilia to 'come home'. Jessica said: "Lillia, you're not in any trouble, I'm really, really worried. It's been four nights now and you need to be safe. Please come home, we all love you very much." GMP yesterday (Thursday) set up a Major Incident Public Portal for information on her whereabouts as detectives again pleaded for information. Officers say it is unclear how long she was on the bus from the Trafford Centre for or where she got off That sighting is being treated as an important part of the investigation, with cops asking for anybody who was on the bus and remembers seeing Lillia to get in touch. Lillia is 5 ft 5; of slim build; with brown hair and glasses. She was last seen wearing a black zip-up hooded top GMP's Major Incident Public Portal can be accessed HERE

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Leigh Guided Busway Major road closed as Tyldesley residents face fortnight of disruption Drivers have been warned to expect delays Comments News Emma Gill Parents editor 18:45, 01 Sep 2026 Updated 19:24, 01 Sep 2026 View 4 Images Astley Street in Tyl One of Tyldesley's busiest roads has shut completely for two weeks as works are carried out on a new travel hub Drivers have been warned to expect delays as Astley Street is closed in both directions close to Leigh Guided Busway until the middle of September. Traffic has already been widely impacted with delays along Hough Lane and other nearby roads Buses are still running along the route as the closure is to 'allow essential utility works as part of the new Tyldesley travel hub, which will add an extra 99 parking bays at the site, aiming to address concerns from residents and local traders about on-street parking in the tow A letter from Transport for Greater Manchester to residents living nearby said: “As part of the next phase of construction, Astley Street will be closed to vehicles immediately north of the guided busway from August 31 to September 14." The existing park and ride facility remains open and bus services are running as usual, but there are concerns about the disruption the road closure is causing and questions over why it's happening on the week children return to school for the new academic year

He went on to smash a couple of windows within the school before fleeing to a neighbouring house. No Metrolink services were running between Wythenshawe Town Centre and Manchester Airport for around an hour this morning (September 14) It followed a crash between a bike and a tram on Shadowmoss Road, near to Shadowmoss tram stop, in Wythenshawe. Greater Manchester Police says it was called out to the scene at 8.22am The force says minor injuries were reported following the incident. Hackers accessed data relating to car park, lounge and fast track bookings and in-airport WIFI s The data included people's email addresses, phone numbers, vehicle registrations and postcodes. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Strangeways Sources speak out on Strangeways' future in Manchester amid 'super prison' plans Strangeways could leave Manchester city centre forever View 3 Images There have long been calls to move Strangeways out of Manchester (Image: Sean Hansford | Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter and Damon Wilkinson Reporter 05:30, 06 Sep 2026 Updated 07:09, 06 Sep 2026 Plans for a new 'super prison' in the North West could help pave the way for the eventual closure of Strangeways , the Manchester Evening News understand This week Andy Burnham's government announced the contract for a new 1,700-place jail in Leyland, Lancs had been signed. It was part of a wider drive to 'ensure the country never again faces the nightmare of running out of prison spaces' But well-placed sources here in Manchester hope the move could help town hall bosses bolster their case for the potential closure of Strangeways. It comes three months after the MEN revealed that 'promising conversations' had been taking place with government about relocating the Speaking this week, Cheetham councillor Naeem Hassan welcomed the announcement of the new prison and said he hopes it helps usher in the end of Strangeways He said: "It's such a prime location in the city. I really want to see it moved. Prisons shouldn't be in city centres, it's not the right place. They should be in rural locations

evidence_packet.evidence_text: OIdham council responds to questions around nightmare road where 125 illegal cars were spotted in one night Videos posted online have claimed up to 125 cars were parked illegally from 1pm to 8pm at night Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Rep Oldham Council has revealed how many fines have been paid on a road that turns into a ‘nightmare’ because people flout the rules. The Manchester Evening News understands issues are still ongoing despite enforcement action Waterloo Street in Oldham cuts through the centre of the suburb of Glodwick but in recent months, it’s been the centre of a debate as cars park repeatedly on double yellow lines, roads are blocked, and the pavements are taken over. Videos posted online have claimed up to 125 cars When the Manchester Evening News went to visit the road in August, multiple cars could be seen parking on the double yellow lines along the entire length and one man said: “People here do not give a s***’. Cars could also be seen parked on grass verges too damaging a nearby green Rafit Hussain, a local business owner and chairman of local political party the Oldham Group, said the lack of public transport links was making the issue worse and called for more awareness and education He also said: “The traffic wardens need to do their job. It’s simple. They are not doing a good job with it.”

The scheme, recommended to be approved by Trafford council’s planning committee next week, would see the existing structures demolished and two blocks of 286 fl One of the blocks would reach 16-storeys in height and contain 192 homes. Just seven vehicle spaces are proposed, which would be disabled spaces. Some 286 cycle spaces would also be offered Residents have branded this offering ‘insufficient’, saying there is already a ‘lack of parking’ in the area. Between Southall Street and what is now the AO Arena the 59-year-old Sikh, known as Gyani Ji, was stopped and ticketed seven times His crime was refusing to remove his turban to wear a helmet while riding his 50cc Honda moped. And his small but persistent acts of civil disobedience would result in a landmark change in the law Gyani Ji was an activist who played a pivotal role in advancing Sikh religious rights in the UK. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Homelessness Rough sleeping rises in Greater Manchester as Andy Burnham pledges to end crisis by Christmas The number of rough sleepers across Greater Manchester went up in June, new figures show, as Prime Minister Andy Burnham vows to get every rough Comments News Paul Gallagher 05:57, 14 Sep 2026 The number of people sleeping rough across Greater Manchester has reached one of its highest levels in six years, according to new data released as former mayor Andy Burnham pledged to make homelessness a national priority Government data shows there were 444 rough sleepers across the ten boroughs of Greater Manchester in June 2026, up from 402 in June 2025 - a rise of 42 people, or 10.4 per cent. It is the highest figure for June, and the fourth highest monthly total since October 2020 The figures land as Mr Burnham - who made ending rough sleeping his first pledge on entering Downing Street in July - is pushing ahead with a national drive to get every rough sleeper off the streets by Christmas , backed by a £442 million funding package The biggest driver of the rise in Greater Manchester was Manchester city itself, where the number of rough sleepers in June jumped from 149 last summer to 195 - an increase of 46 people Tameside saw the second sharpest rise, climbing from 21 to 33, while Trafford rose from 6 to 10 and Bury edged up from 29 to 31. Not all boroughs saw increases. Salford , Oldham , Rochdale and Bolton recorded slightly lower numbers sleeping rough on their streets

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Police His stark grave says 'you didn't deserve to go this way' - now GMP are reinvestigating his murder Coroner calls for police review into the death of 43-year-old found in undergrowth after witnesses claim a 'conspiracy of silen Comments News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 05:52, 15 Sep 2026 Updated 06:24, 15 Sep 2026 A week before Christmas in 2024 his family and friends gathered at the Raka Raka bar and restaurant in Salford . The venue on Cottenham Lane lies in the middle of a sprawl of industrial units It specialises in Zimbabwean and Southern African cuisine - flame -grilled meats, Boerewors traditional sausage, and staple foods like sadza from ground maize. The bar has imported beer like Hunters Dry and DJs play Afrobeat But the mood was respectful and reflective. Those present were remembering one of their own, Tanyaradzwa Julius Matera The next day, on December 18, many of them also attended his funeral at Peel Green Cemetery chapel followed by burial nearby in a tree-lined plot. His final resting place is more than 5,000 miles from his homeland A simple grey cross marks his grave and on the plaque bearing his name is embossed with: "You didn't deserve to go this way. Rest in Peace"

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Stockport Stockport care home boss says 'I didn't think a human could fit through' after gran falls to death from bedroom window The inquest into the death of 78-year-old Maureen O'Callaghan is being heard at Stockport Coroners' Court View 2 Images Ma News Chris Slater Senior Reporter 06:10, 18 Sep 2026 The former manager of a care home where a beloved gran fell to her death from her bedroom window - having previously attempted to climb through - told an inquest he did not believe a 'human being could fit through' Maureen O'Callaghan, who had dementia, died at Berrycroft Manor in Romiley, Stockport, on September 29 last year. The 78-year-old fell through her upstairs bedroom window, having previously attempted to climb out and throwing items from it Ms O'Callaghan's loved ones have told an inquest into her death, being heard at Stockport Coroners' Court, they believe her death was a 'preventable tragedy' Coroner Jyoti Gillearlier earlier heard Ms O'Callaghan moved to Berrycroft Manor in January 2025 to benefit from '24-hour care' at a cost of '£1,600 a week'. Her family said they had spoken to care home staff with safety concerns about the window, but nothing was done about Describing Ms O'Callaghan's death as a 'preventable tragedy', the family said: "She was an integral part of our close family and her loss will stay with us all."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Stockport Stockport council accused of U-turn after plan to increase bin collections Stockport council’s leadership has been accused of ‘making policy on the back of a fag packet’ News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 07:42, 29 Aug 2026 View Ima Stockport council’s leadership has been accused of ‘making policy on the back of a fag packet’ following a major bin announcement. But top councillors said there would be no cuts to services as a result of the change From the beginning of December 2026, blue bins for paper and cardboard recycling will be collected every two weeks instead of every four weeks across Stockport . The council moved to four weekly collections due to financial pressures on its budget for day-to-day services in 2025 Earlier this week, councillor Jake Austin, who is the cabinet member overseeing bin services, said he was delighted to announce the move and feedback had been ‘loud and clear’ that people ‘want a service that makes it easier to recycle’ Council leader Mark Roberts said: “It is critical people know the Liberal Democrats will listen to the feedback given and strive to make a positive difference wherever we can.” The announcement this week has come after weeks of criticism of the local authority . evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Stockport murderer who kidnapped girl off street and sexually attacked her in horror eight-hour ordeal jailed for life Paul Sharpe held his victim hostage for eight hours before they were found by police in a hotel car park News Stephen Topping A convicted murderer who kidnapped a girl at knifepoint before sexually assaulting her has been jailed for life. Paul Sharpe held his 15-year-old victim hostage during a grim eight-hour ordeal, as he drove from one car park to another The 56-year-old put the girl in a headlock and bundled her into his car on Bradgate Road, in Altrincham , at around 7.30pm on May 18 - claiming that her father owed him money. He drove to a car park at Manchester Airport and tied up her ankles and wrists with a neck tie That night, he drove to different car parks in Greater Manchester and Cheshire, and plied the girl with alcohol while sexually assaulting her. At one point, former radio DJ Sharpe masturbated while touching the girl's feet, the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) said He was finally caught by police in a hotel car park in Knutsford at around 3.40am on May 19. The girl had been reported as missing by her mother, while CCTV allowed officers to identify Sharpe's car, according to the CPS Greater Manchester Police says the girl had been studying at Sale Library on May 18 before beginning her journey home with friends at around 5:50pm. At 6:10pm, she contacted her parents to let them know she was on her way home

Officers from Greater Manchester Police were called to reports of the serious incident at around 6pm on Saturday, August 19, at the restaurant on Riverside Walk A boy, aged 13, was taken to hospital with serious injuries. Two teenage boys have since been arrested on suspicion of assault and possession of a bladed article. Enquiries are ongoing, GMP say A man and his family, who were dining at the restaurant, witnessed the incident. Speaking to the Manchester Evening News , David Lane told of the 'horrific moment' and how his actions helped save the boy "We sat down and ordered our food at around 5.50pm, then a load of kids came in and started fighting," he said. "I got up and went to one of the crew members at Taco Bell and asked them to kick them out because my family were there "I told them to lock the door, and they never did. About ten minutes later, the crew member who was guarding the door was pushed by one of them, then around 20 to 25 youths ran in, some with knives."

He searched for details on the Manchester attack, which claimed the lives of Melvin Cravitz, 66, and Adrian Daulby, 53, before placing a The 19-year-old then filmed himself 'triggering' the modified vest, overlaying the sound of an explosion over the video. After Nadir was arrested in October 2025, police found the weighted vest in his wardrobe, handwritten texts promoting martyrdom operations and a large quantity of terrorist CTPNE said this material included Daesh propaganda videos, and texts calling for the killing of 'disbelievers'. They were remanded to custody for an additional week as police continue their investigation Last week (September 7) the pair were charged with going equipped to cause criminal damage, namely with lighter fuel and spray paint, and possession of an offensive weapon, namely a hammer and a kitchen knife Police said that officers were called to Singleton Road in Salford at 1.50am on Sunday (September 6). Neighbours describe having had multiple cars written off over the years, on a street likened to a 'race track'

Sheila Rowan, 70, was knocked down by Sohail Aurangzeb in his partner's Nissan Juke, which he took without her permission on the afternoon of Au Aurangzeb, 42, had no driving licence and wasn't insured. He said he got lost and drove onto a rural, cobbled road in Ashton-under-Lyne. He claimed he drove into a ditch, which caused the car to swerve and hit Mrs Rowan Manchester Crown Court heard Aurangzeb drove away and didn't report the incident. Mrs Rowan was found by passers-by who called 999. She died in hospital later that day Aurangzeb was jailed for seven years and four months on Friday (September 4). He earlier pleaded guilty to aggravated vehicle taking, with court documents stating Ms Rowan's death was 'caused by accident' Recorder Andrew Vinson told him: "You have shown a deliberate disregard for the safety of others. You had not passed your driving test; you had not driven that car before; you were not insured; and you did not have a driving licence. You have shown no remorse or concern."
